facts: I built a Unix-like shell (SXSHELL) in C to understand more about the terminal I use every day.
I enjoy game development and experimenting with gameplay ideas in Godot and Unity.
I’m fascinated by the connection between high-level backend engineering and low-level systems programming.
A good debugging session with GDB or Valgrind teaches me more than a dozen pages of notes.

interests.title: Things I like learning about
interests.intro: I like understanding how a thing works, not just learning how to use it. These are the areas I keep coming back to.

items.title: Java backend development
items.description: I’m learning how backend applications are structured, how APIs communicate, and how data moves reliably between an application and a database. My current direction is Core Java, SQL, and Spring Boot.

items.title: Systems programming

items.Highlight: Building tools from scratch—like a POSIX shell, an HTTP server, and a mark-and-sweep garbage collector—to demystify OS internals.

projects.title: Projects and experiments
projects.intro: I learn best by making things, testing them, and figuring out the parts I don’t understand yet. Here are the projects and experiments from that process.

items.title: SXSHELL
items.description: A Unix-like shell written from scratch in C. It supports built-in commands, PATH-based command lookup, quoting and escaping, I/O redirection, multi-command pipelines, persistent history, and shell variable expansion.
items.learning: Built to understand process management, file descriptors, and the system calls behind terminal commands.
underTheHood: Uses fork(), execvp(), waitpid(), pipe(), and dup2() for process execution and multi-stage pipelines
Custom tokenizer handling single/double quotes, backslash escaping, and environment variable expansion
Persistent command history and signal handling (SIGINT) so Ctrl+C interrupts child processes without killing the shell

items.title: Custom HTTP Server
items.description: A lightweight HTTP/1.1 server in C, currently in progress, focused on using raw TCP sockets and learning how requests are received, parsed, and answered.
items.learning: The goal is to learn more about networking fundamentals by implementing the request-response flow directly.
underTheHood: POSIX socket lifecycle: socket(), bind(), listen(), accept(), recv(), and send()
Zero-dependency HTTP request line, header parser, and status-code response builder
Static file serving with MIME type detection and concurrent client connection handling

items.title: Custom Garbage Collector
items.description: A custom garbage collector in C built to understand manual memory management, heap allocation internals, and automatic object reachability tracking.
items.learning: Explores mark-and-sweep collection, root pointer tracing, and allocation metadata at the pointer level.
underTheHood: Tracks dynamically allocated objects via an intrusive metadata header and allocation list
Mark phase traverses reachable object graphs from registered stack/root pointers
Sweep phase reclaims unmarked heap blocks and prevents memory leaks

items.title: Git Implementation in C
items.description: A simplified Git clone written in C to understand content-addressable storage, blob and tree objects, and commit history DAGs.
items.learning: Covers binary file I/O, cryptographic hashing, compression, and version control internals from scratch.
underTheHood: Implements object hashing and content-addressable storage inside .git/objects
Reads and writes blob, tree, and commit objects with header framing
Demystifies how Git snapshots file trees rather than storing simple line diffs

items.title: E-commerce Backend API
items.description: A complete e-commerce REST backend built with Spring Boot, featuring product catalog management, order workflows, JWT authentication, and pagination.
items.learning: Focused on enterprise backend architecture, relational database modeling, and clean service-layer separation.
underTheHood: Layered Spring Boot architecture (Controller → Service → Repository) with Spring Data JPA
Stateless JWT authentication, role-based access control, and request validation
PostgreSQL schema with indexed queries and paginated product endpoints

items.title: Expense Tracker API
items.description: A secure REST API for personal expense tracking, demonstrating robust CRUD operations, category analytics, Spring Security integration, and Docker containerization.
items.learning: Built to practice API security beyond the happy path, error handling, and containerized deployment.
underTheHood: Spring Security filter chain with BCrypt password hashing and user-scoped data isolation
Normalized SQL schema for transactions, recurring budgets, and monthly aggregations
Docker Compose setup bundling the Spring Boot service and PostgreSQL database

about.title: Learning by making things
about.intro: I’m Shiva, a Bachelor of Computer Applications student at Amity University Online. This page is a small introduction, along with my academic background and current focus.
approachParagraphs: I enjoy projects that force me to look beyond the surface. Building SXSHELL made me think carefully about parsing input, launching processes, handling file descriptors, and dealing with errors.
My current professional direction is Java backend development. Alongside it, systems programming helps me strengthen my understanding of what software depends on underneath.
I also make games as a creative outlet. Switching between backend code, low-level systems work, and game development gives me different ways to solve problems.
